title: The pronuclei travel curved paths and meet before reaching the centre of the egg

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The pronuclei travel curved paths and meet before reaching the centre of the egg

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Given an attraction between the male and female pronuclei and a force drawing them toward the egg centre, their paths lie within the triangle formed by the two bodies and the centre, are curved (convex toward the line joining them) unless they start on a diameter, and the pronuclei meet a little before the centre and then travel straight to it.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: (2) unless the two bodies happen to lie, to begin with, precisely on a diameter of the cell, their paths until they meet one another will be curved paths, the convexity of the curve being towards the straight line joining the two bodies; (3) the two bodies will meet a little before they reach the centre;

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Fertilisation and the pronuclei”. Scope: pronuclear migration in fertilised eggs (e.g. frog)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-11: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This prediction specifies observable trajectory geometry and a direct refuting result. Standard segmentation and tracking can test it in public time-lapse datasets, although exact species coverage may be limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Segment male and female pronuclei and the egg center in 3D time-lapse fertilization movies, then measure path curvature, convexity, meeting position, and post-meeting trajectory. The stated geometry is confirmed if non-diametric starts produce the predicted curves and precentral meeting consistently; contrary trajectories refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public datasets may emphasize model organisms other than frogs.

Projection of 3D paths into 2D can bias curvature.

discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is geometric and sharp, and fertilization movies in public archives contain the paths for several model eggs. Turning movies into a confirm-or-refute test still takes tracking, and the species mix only partly matches the eggs Thompson had in mind. The curvature and meeting-point criteria do discriminate this two-force picture from a straight mutual approach.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track male and female pronuclei from sperm entry until they meet, and test three predictions: paths stay inside the triangle they form with the egg centre, curves are convex toward the line joining the pronuclei unless they start on a diameter, and they meet before the centre and only then move straight to it. That geometry would support the claim; straight paths, or a meeting at or beyond the centre, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Meeting before the centre can arise from more than one force law.

Public movies are concentrated on nematode, mouse and echinoderm eggs rather than the frog geometry Thompson illustrated.

Ready-made coordinate tables are rarer than the movies.
